content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want an angular plate with two quadratic plates positioned in right angel to each other. The edge length of the plates is 140mm. They are 10mm thick. On one of the two plates I would like to have a quadratic cutout, 45x45mm, centred on the plate. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation (using the functions namespace only)

1. Establish the coordinate system  
   • All dimensions are given in millimetres.  
   • The global origin (0 ,0 ,0) will be the common inside corner where the two plates meet.  
   • Positive X, Y and Z axes point along the length, width and height directions, respectively.

2. Create the first plate (horizontal plate in the XY-plane)  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Base point: (0 ,0 ,0).  
   • Because this is the very first solid, its subtraction flag must be False.

3. Create the second plate (vertical plate in the YZ-plane, perpendicular to the first)  
   • Geometry: 10 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base point: (0 ,0 ,0) – this lets the two plates share the same inside edge and guarantees they are connected.  
   • Subtraction flag is also False (it adds material).

4. Define the quadratic cut-out in the first plate  
   • The cut-out is 45 mm × 45 mm and must pierce the full 10 mm thickness of the first plate.  
   • To centre it on the 140 mm × 140 mm plate, place its base point at  
     x = (140 − 45)/2 = 47.5 mm,  
     y = (140 − 45)/2 = 47.5 mm,  
     z = 0 mm.  
   • Geometry for the subtractive block: 45 mm (X) × 45 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Set the subtraction flag to True so this block removes material.

5. Combine all three blocks in one call to functions.block by supplying three-element arrays:  
   • x_size  = [140,  10, 45]  
   • y_size  = [140, 140, 45]  
   • z_size  = [ 10, 140, 10]  
   • x       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   • y       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   • z       = [  0,   0,   0]  
   • subtraction = [False, False, True]

6. (Optional) End with a single functions.finished call to indicate that all geometry calls have been supplied.

When you are ready, ask me to prepare the exact function call; I will then output the functions.block (…) and functions.finished (…) calls but will not execute them until you explicitly instruct me to do so.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
